UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile in the FinTrack Personal application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

userId.description: The ID of the user who owns this transaction.

date.description: The date and time of the transaction.

userId.description: The ID of the user who owns this goal.

name.description: The name of the goal (e.g., 'Vacation Fund').

targetAmount.description: The target amount to save for the goal.

currentAmount.description: The current amount saved towards the goal.

createdAt.description: Timestamp for when the goal was created.

userId.description: The ID of the user who owns this subscription.

amount.description: The amount paid for the subscription.

startDate.description: The date the subscription started or the next payment is due.

userId.description: The ID of the user (teacher) who owns this student record.

balance.description: The student's current financial balance. Positive is credit, negative is debt.

lessonPrice.description: The price of a single lesson for this student.

createdAt.description: Timestamp for when the student was added.

LessonLog.title: LessonLog
LessonLog.description: Represents a log of a completed lesson for a student.

userId.description: The ID of the user (teacher) who owns this lesson log.

studentId.description: The ID of the student who took the lesson.

date.description: Timestamp for when the lesson was completed.

lessonPrice.description: The price of the completed lesson.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to manage user-specific data securely and efficiently under a single `/users/{userId}` document tree. This path-based ownership model provides excellent security and simplifies rules. Subcollections like transactions, goals, subscriptions, and students are nested under each user to enforce ownership and for data locality. This facilitates simple, robust, and easily debuggable security rules. There is no denormalized authorization data.
